what_happens: Check whether the agency already posts the records on its website
legal_basis: FOIA.gov, How do I make a FOIA request?
source_words: Before making a request, first look to see if the information you are interested in is already publicly available.

what_happens: Send the agency’s FOIA office a written request that reasonably describes the records, following the agency’s published rules; no special form is needed
source_words: upon any request for records which (i) reasonably describes such records and (ii) is made in accordance with published rules stating the time, place, fees (if any), and procedures to be followed

step: Say what fees you will pay
what_happens: Commercial requesters pay for search, copying and review; schools, scientific institutions and news media pay for copying only; everyone else pays for search and copying, with the first two hours of search and the first 100 pages free. Ask for a waiver when release serves the public interest
source_words: for the first two hours of search time or for the first one hundred pages of duplication

what_happens: Ask for expedited processing with a certified statement of compelling need: a threat to someone’s life or safety, or, for a person whose main work is informing the public, urgency to inform the public about federal government activity
time_limit: The agency decides whether to expedite within 10 days
source_words: within 10 days after the date of the request

what_happens: The agency decides whether to release the records and says why, with the right to appeal and to ask its FOIA Public Liaison or the Office of Government Information Services for help
time_limit: 20 working days, and up to 10 more in unusual circumstances
source_words: determine within 20 days (excepting Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) after the receipt of any such request

what_happens: Appeal to the head of the agency
time_limit: At least 90 days to appeal; the agency decides within 20 working days
source_words: not less than 90 days after the date of such adverse determination

what_happens: The National Archives’ Office of Government Information Services mediates disputes, as an alternative to a lawsuit
source_words: The Office of Government Information Services shall offer mediation services to resolve disputes between persons making requests under this section and administrative agencies as a nonexclusive alternative to litigation

what_happens: Sue in federal district court; a requester whose agency misses the time limits may sue without finishing the appeal
source_words: shall be deemed to have exhausted his administrative remedies with respect to such request if the agency fails to comply with the applicable time limit provisions of this paragraph
